summary: Decoded Global/PartitionTable (a one-entry workset table) and the full framing of Partitions/<N> (18-byte header, 26-byte block headers, gzip members with valid trailers, 6-byte block trailers, save-unit footers/separators, end record), and discovered a corpus-wide stream paging layer (64,896-byte pages each followed by a 353-byte opaque page trailer) that explains every 'corrupt gzip trailer' in the corpus: after de-paging, 13,535/13,535 gzip members validate against their CRC32/ISIZE and Formats/Latest inflates to exactly its stored 496,597 bytes. Element data is three parallel logical record streams (seq 101/102/103) chunked into ~128 KiB blocks; records span blocks; concatenated segments walk 100% as [16- or 20-byte header][body] records in all 21 segments, with identical record counts per segment. Delivered src/rvt/partitions.py (PartitionTable parser, depage(), stream/framing walker, iter_blocks, concat_elements, scan_element_headers, __main__ report over all six files), docs/streams/05-partitions.md (layouts, worked hex, correlation tables, confidence, unknowns) and docs/inbox/partitions.md (paging fix + cross-slice findings).
key_findings: CORPUS-WIDE: every OLE stream payload is stored as 64,896-byte (0xFD80) pages, each full page followed by a 353-byte opaque page-trailer (first byte 0x00, second a multiple of 0x10). Removing them at raw offsets 64896 + k*65249 makes 100% of gzip members validate (13,535/13,535 in all seven Partitions streams) and yields Formats/Latest = exactly ISIZE 496,597 bytes with matching CRC 0x26852216 — the current extracted/*.gz/NNN.bin corpus is silently garbled past any page boundary (e.g. schema inflated as 498,766 bytes).

Global/PartitionTable = workset table, NOT a partition index: u16 class ordinal 0x0c80, u32 version 1, u32 count (1 in every sample), then per entry GUID(16), u32 0, u32 id_a (352/254/131), u32 id_b (824/596/776/556/989/2654), i32 -1, u32 kind (0 user, 1 'Project Standards', 2 'Family : Title Blocks : A0 metric'), u8 0, u32 name_len + UTF-16 name ('Workset1'/'Architektur'), then u32 1,1,0,1,0. Four template-born files share workset GUID {E3E052F8-0156-11D5-9301-0000863F27AD}.

Partitions/<N>: N is the document-increment counter — Global/DocumentIncrementTable's first u32 = max(N)+1 in all six files (16/14/15/13/22/86); dach kept two partitions, /85 being an empty later one (0 elements, 3 sentinel records, 291 bytes) which serves as the fully-annotated reference example.
Stream header (18 B, de-paged): u32 9, u32 0, u16 0x3a3, i32 0, u32 elem_table_count (equals the count field of Global/ElemTable: 8401/17231/13855/13936/49776). It does not index the gzip blocks.

Block framing: u16 0x0f28, u32 flags (4 whole records, 6 last record continues, 7 pure continuation, 5 continuation ends), u32 A (record headers starting here), u32 B (= 8 + gzip member length; mirrored in trailer, 100% after de-paging), u32 C, u32 seq (101/102/103), u32 0, gzip member (10-B header, raw deflate, valid crc32/isize), u16 0x0f21 + u32 B trailer. ISIZE == hdr_len(seq)*A + C + adj with adj = {4:0, 6:-4, 7:0, 5:+4}, exact on all 13,535 blocks.

Save units: blocks are grouped into units (racbasic 164, dach/84 1,244); unit 0 = original save, later units ~one 101/102/103 block each. Each unit ends with an 18-byte terminator (0x0f28 + zeros), a 0x0f3f-tagged 64-byte opaque blob (0 bytes in dach/85), a u32-len UTF-16 'Data generated by Autodesk® Revit®', then a 28-byte separator (a3 03, -1, a2 03, u32 counter, 16-byte GUID) before the next unit; the stream ends with an 'a3 03 0 -1 0' record, zero padding and a 48–276-byte high-entropy tail. Separator GUIDs recur in Global/Latest (2x) and Global/ContentDocuments (1x).

Element data = three parallel logical record streams (seq 101/102/103) chopped into ~128 KiB gzip blocks; records DO span block boundaries (flags 6->7->5 chains, e.g. a 487,202-byte KeynoteTable record over racbasic blocks 12–15); pure concatenation of block payloads per seq yields a contiguous [header][body] record stream that walks 100% in all 21 segments (racbasic: 15.3 MB/85,978 records in 101, 63.9 MB in 102, 28.5 MB in 103; identical record count and id set per segment).

Record framing: seq 101 = 16-byte header {i64 id, u32 body_size, u32 cls_word}, cls 0x5e5 (~ElementHeader) for every record; seq 102/103 = 20-byte header {i64 id, u32 stamp, u32 body_size, u32 cls_word}; seq 102 = the polymorphic element objects (top classes 2252/737/954/2572/2124/1158 ~ GStyleElem/CategoryElem/CurveElem/LinearDimensionType/FontTable/DBViewType), seq 103 = 86–90% class 0x0f2c (~SerializedDummy, 2-byte body) + 0x89e (~GElement). One sentinel record with id -1, cls 0 per save unit per segment.

Ids: partition records use ids up to 1,098,851 (85,815 distinct in racbasic); Global/ElemTable (8,401 x 40-byte records after 'c9 05 <count>') is a subset (8,223 of its ids occur in partition records); element 86291 is racbasic block 0's first record and is present in ElemTable.

Stream-lead u16 class ordinals (drift-corrected ±1, for schema agent): 0x1c ADocument (Global/Latest), 0x5c9 ElemTable, 0x53c DocumentIncrementTable, 0x538 DocumentHistory (History), 0x53e DocumentStorageIndex[Impl] (Contents), 0xc80 PartitionTable, 0x3a2/0x3a3 ContentMarker/ContentRec, and framing tags 0x0f28/0x0f21/0x0f3f ~ SegmentMarker/SegmentCheckback/SignatureMarker.

tools/scan_gzip.py index.json is doubly wrong for partitions: it carved paged bytes (a page trailer inside 15–25% of members made raw+10 fallback output garbage past the trailer) and it missed ~8% of members (racbasic 1068 carved vs 1156 real blocks).
confidence: High for stream paging (64896+353), the PartitionTable byte layout, the Partitions framing (header/block/trailer/unit/end-record layouts), the flags/ISIZE relation, record framing and the three-parallel-segment model — all verified with 100% CRC/ISIZE validation and 100% record-walk coverage across all six files (seven partition streams, 13,535 blocks). Medium (hypothesis, ±1 drift) for schema class-ordinal names. Low/unknown for the semantics of the 353-byte page trailer, the 64-byte 0x0f3f footer blob, the end-record entropy tail, the seq-102/103 'stamp' field, the separator counter, and PartitionTable id_a/id_b.
open_questions: What is inside the 353-byte page trailer (byte0=0x00, byte1 multiple of 0x10, 351 high-entropy bytes) — checksum, MAC or signature? A writer (Epic D) must reproduce it, so it needs an owner.
What is the 64-byte blob after tag 0x0f3f in each save-unit footer (candidate class name SignatureMarker) and the 48–276-byte high-entropy tail after the stream end record?

Semantics of the u32 'stamp' field in seq 102/103 record headers (per-record, not crc32/adler32 of the body; constant 0x0069003c on small seq-103 records) and of the u32 separator 'counter' (185–4633).
Meaning of PartitionTable id_a (352/254/131) and id_b (824/596/776/556/989/2654; 824 recurs in racbasic DocumentIncrementTable next to a user name).

Exact class-ordinal enumeration of Formats/Latest (my first-occurrence scan drifts +1 above ordinal ~250) to firm up the class names of stream leads (0x3a3, 0x5c9, 0x0c80, 0x0f28/0x0f21/0x0f3f, 0x5e5, 0x0f2c...) — schema agent (A2), now unblocked by de-paging.

Why three segments carry identical record counts/id sets: what exactly are seq 101 (ElementHeader-class records), 102 (element objects) and 103 (SerializedDummy/GElement) at the object-model level, and how do modified elements get versioned across the 164+ appended save units (each id appears exactly once per segment)?
Internal record body structure (nested {u16 class, u32 1, i64 self-id} sub-objects, the 48x0xff prefix in ElementHeader records) — needs the schema field lists to type-decode.
next_steps: Orchestrator: merge docs/inbox/partitions.md into KNOWLEDGE.md — the 64,896+353 paging is corpus-wide; add depage() to tools (new scan step) and re-carve every stream's gzip members from de-paged bytes, validating each with its now-real CRC32/ISIZE (do not edit tools/scan_gzip.py from an analysis slice; assign it).

Notify the schema agent (A2) that Formats/Latest de-paged inflates to 496,597 clean bytes (all garbled late class names were paging artefacts) and ask for an exact ordinal->class enumeration to confirm the stream-lead/framing-tag names listed in 05-partitions §7.

Notify A4 (ElemTable), A5 (Global/Latest), A7 (ContentDocuments/History) agents: their large streams cross page boundaries and their current inflated .gz members are corrupt past the first boundary; also share that stream leads are u16 class ordinals and that partition unit GUIDs appear in Latest/ContentDocuments.

Next decoding target in this slice: type-decode record bodies (start with seq-101 ElementHeader records and the nested {class, version, self-id} object headers) using the schema field lists once A2 exports them; cross-map cls_word values to schema classes at scale.

Extend rvt.partitions into the planned rvt package (A11): expose a Partition/segment reader that other decoders can consume (records_by_id map across the three segments), and add regression asserts (block count, 100% CRC, 100% segment walk) as the E1 verify harness for this slice.

Investigate the page trailer and 0x0f3f blob formats (needed for Epic D writing): collect all 3,282 page trailers plus footer blobs across files and test hypotheses (SHA/HMAC/CRC families over the preceding page, RSA/ECDSA signature blocks).
